messages:
maria: Heads-up — after rolling out the "pack-by-latency" continuous-batching heuristic at 02:00, we see 95p tail for small chat requests jump ~120ms on dedicated pools. Not widespread but reproducible on g4dn-pool-3.

alex: saw it on our dashboards too. 95/99 both moved. Throughput looks fine, it's a latency tail thing.

jin: pinging infra-bot for deploy markers — did the rollout include any kernel routing changes?

infra-bot: deploy: rollout pack-by-latency on pool g4dn-pool-3 started at 2026-03-12T02:00:12Z by release/heuristic-v3.4. No kernel changes in this deploy.

noah: I profiled a couple of traces — the runtime is choosing an int8 kernel path for some microbatch shapes that used to pick the fp16 fused attention kernel. That kernel switch costs ~80ms per request due to extra reshapes + suboptimal cuda kernels.

maria: interesting — why would pack-by-latency flip kernel choice?

noah: because packing aggregated longer sequences into the same microbatch more often, leading to different batch-shape distribution; the kernel selector picks based on dominant shape and memory estimate. Short requests occasionally get coalesced into a shape combo with a long request and the selector picks the slower but memory-saving path.

alex: KV cache behavior also looks off — cache hit rate dips by ~3% for affected model version. Could be eviction churn from mixed length sequences.

jin: attaching a sampled trace and the selector decision log: 
```
TRACE: req=0x7f3a, seq_len=28, packed_with=[req=0x9c2b seq_len=512], chosen_kernel=int8_mixed_stride, expected_latency=120ms
KERNELS_PROF: int8_mixed_stride: p50=30ms p95=110ms, fp16_fused: p50=12ms p95=25ms
KV: hit_before=0.942 hit_after=0.909
```

maria: ugh, that gap explains the tail. Any quick mitigation?

noah: two levers we can flip quickly: 1) add an age-based bypass so requests older than X ms get served ASAP (skip pack-by-latency), 2) adjust token_budget_target so small requests avoid co-packing with huge ones.

alex: i'd prefer trying the age bypass first (lower blast radius). Implement a 15ms age cutoff for latency-sensitive routes (.chat-latency).

jin: PR opened: `runtime: bypass packer for age_ms >= 15 for routes matching chat-latency` — roll out to g4dn-pool-3 in canary now.

infra-bot: canary rollout started to subset 10% of hosts in g4dn-pool-3.

noah: after canary we should also monitor kernel selection histograms — add a short profiler that samples kernel choice vs batch-shape. I have a snippet to log shape->kernel mapping.

maria: can someone run an ad-hoc perf job reproducer? I'll compare with baseline.

alex: running replay with 100k small chat requests + 10% long tails now, will post results in ~10m.

(noah posts): profiler snippet: 
```
// Pseudolog
batch_shape: [16x28, 1x512] -> dominant_shape=512 -> kernel=int8_mixed_stride
batch_shape: [16x28] -> kernel=fp16_fused
```

alex: canary numbers after 12m: 95p latency for chat-latency route on canary hosts down to baseline +5ms (was +120ms). KV hit rate recovered to -0.5% vs baseline.

maria: great. what's the plan for full rollback vs permanent change?

noah: proposal: keep age-bypass for latency-sensitive routes and add a shape-aware token_budget tweak that prevents co-packing of tiny reqs with huge ones unless it improves p95. Also add kernel-selection telemetry to the console (per-route kernel histograms).

jin: i'll open a follow-up RFC for the shape-aware budget and telemetry work. Include an experiment to try a kernel-preference bias: prefer fp16_fused when a threshold of small requests present.

alex: agree. For now keep canary promoting to 50% while we review the RFC.

maria: thanks all — timeline: promote canary to 50% in 30m, RFC by EOD, and a full pool rollout (with metrics gated) tomorrow. Adding todo to follow-up thread. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: rollout: canary -> 50% started at 2026-03-12T03:05:00Z

noah: postmortem note: root cause = pack-by-latency changed batch-shape distribution -> kernel selector picked memory-saving int8 kernel for mixed batches -> increased per-request latency for small requests; contributing = KV eviction churn from mixed sequence lengths.

maria: tagging @product and @eng-sre for visibility.
